about: Cases for the lock screen's caption lines, read by both OzenKitTests (LockScreenSharedCasesTests, Swift) and core LockScreenSharedCasesTest (Kotlin). A letter is what a reader sees as one: a Hindi syllable with its vowel sign, a letter with its vowel points or accent, an emoji. tail is LockScreenCaptions.tail; lines is LockScreenCaptions.lines over the segments (id n is the UUID 00000000-0000-0000-0000-n padded to 12 digits; speaker is a key of names; start and end in seconds, default 0; committed defaults to true). Hindi conjuncts (a virama joining two consonants) are left out: Java 21 still splits them into two letters, while the iPhone and Android 15 keep them as one (Unicode 15.1).
